claims.text: A refractory-element-containing high-entropy alloy will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared with conventional structural alloys.
The superior degradation resistance will result from formation of a stable protective oxide film under elevated-temperature wear conditions.
The proposed HEA is homogenized and has a single-phase or near-single-phase solid-solution structure.
The proposed HEA contains multiple principal elements, including refractory metals.
Combined elevated temperature, mechanical wear, and corrosive exposure will produce a stable, adherent oxide layer on the HEA.
The HEA will possess a fine microstructure with sluggish diffusion characteristics under the proposed conditions.
The adherent oxide layer and sluggish-diffusion microstructure will mitigate surface damage and corrosion propagation.
A multi-principal-element composition encourages formation of complex oxide scales at high temperature.
The complex oxide scales act as barriers to corrosion.
The complex oxide scales act as barriers to wear.
Refractory components enhance the thermal stability of the HEA.
Refractory components reduce elemental diffusion rates and thereby slow degradation.
Under identical tribo-corrosion conditions, the HEA will have a lower mass-loss rate than conventional structural alloys.
Under identical tribo-corrosion conditions, the HEA will retain hardness better than conventional structural alloys.
Under identical tribo-corrosion conditions, the HEA will exhibit lower friction than conventional structural alloys.
The expected performance advantage is limited to the designed temperature and wear regimes.
At drastically higher temperatures or in more aggressive chemical environments, the performance difference may diminish.
